title: The Big Misconception
next: Is the Earth a Prison or a Blessing?

narration: Every day, thousands of ships carry grain, oil and goods across the world's oceans.
Goods flow one way. Money flows the other.
So here is a question. Does the Quran have anything to say about this system?
Welcome to Quran and Global Economy. Episode one: the big misconception.

scenes.source: Based on notes from lectures by Nouman Ali Khan
narration: Before we start, a promise.
This series is based on notes from lectures by Nouman Ali Khan, and every verse has been checked against the Arabic text, a trusted translation, and classical tafsir.
Gold marks the Quran's own words. Brown marks scholarly interpretation. Teal marks a modern application. And coral marks a claim that still needs evidence.
Where the original notes made a mistake, we will stop and correct it.

props.heading: How to watch
props.footer: Mistakes in the source notes are corrected on screen

scenes.source: A common attitude, not a survey result
narration: Many people believe religion is only about prayer and fasting.
Business, careers and the economy? That's worldly, with nothing to do with faith.
But is that what the Quran actually says?
Look at two verses from Surah Al-Jumu'ah.
The first says: when the call to Friday prayer is made, hurry to the remembrance of Allah, and leave trade.

props.arabic: فَٱسۡعَوۡاْ إِلَىٰ ذِكۡرِ ٱللَّهِ وَذَرُواْ ٱلۡبَيۡعَ
props.english: …proceed to the remembrance of Allah and leave trade.

narration: And the very next verse says: when the prayer is over, disperse in the land, and seek from the bounty of Allah.
Leave the market, then return to it. One passage, one day, two movements.
This is why scholars say that, with the right intention, earning a living becomes part of worship.

props.arabic: فَٱنتَشِرُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَٱبۡتَغُواْ مِن فَضۡلِ ٱللَّهِ
props.english: Disperse within the land and seek from the bounty of Allah.
props.highlight: seek from the bounty of Allah
props.note: Earning, with the right intention, is part of worship

narration: The Quran even challenges those who ban good things for themselves.
Say: who has forbidden the adornment of Allah, which He produced for His servants, and the good things of provision?

props.arabic: قُلۡ مَنۡ حَرَّمَ زِينَةَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّتِيٓ أَخۡرَجَ لِعِبَادِهِۦ وَٱلطَّيِّبَٰتِ مِنَ ٱلرِّزۡقِ
props.english: Say, “Who has forbidden the adornment of Allah which He has produced for His servants and the good things of provision?”

narration: The Quran doesn't reject the material world. It organises it.
Seek the home of the Hereafter, but do not forget your share of this world.

props.arabic: وَٱبۡتَغِ فِيمَآ ءَاتَىٰكَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلدَّارَ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةَۖ وَلَا تَنسَ نَصِيبَكَ مِنَ ٱلدُّنۡيَا
props.english: Seek, through what Allah has given you, the home of the Hereafter; and do not forget your share of the world.
props.highlight: do not forget your share of the world

narration: What about leaving the world entirely, and living in isolation?
The Quran says monasticism was something people invented. Allah did not prescribe it.

props.english: …and monasticism, which they innovated; We did not prescribe it for them.

narration: And in Sahih al-Bukhari, the Prophet, peace be upon him, stopped companions who vowed to fast forever and never marry.
He said: whoever turns away from my way is not from me.

props.label: Hadith
props.quote: “Whoever turns away from my Sunnah is not from me.”
props.context: Said to companions who vowed to fast every day, pray all night and never marry

narration: One correction.
The popular line, there is no monasticism in Islam, is not an authentic hadith in that wording.
And the Prophet himself retreated to the cave of Hira. So the point is permanent withdrawal from society, not caves.

props.said: “No monasticism in Islam” as a hadith
props.said2: Sitting in caves is not Islam
props.fix2: Permanent withdrawal from society is rejected

narration: So this series reads the Quran not only for belief and law, like inheritance or divorce,
but through an economic lens.
Next episode: is the earth a prison, or a blessing? Follow for episode two.
